How the hit roll and miss patterns work

Hit probability: Base chance + aim bonus − penalty gives the intended-part hit chance, limited to 5–95%. Natural 20 is a successful roll; natural 1 is a failed roll. The ordinary check is adjusted so those exceptions are included in the displayed chance, not added on top. A success sends a straight ray to the aim point, without scatter. Solid cover can still intercept it.

Miss placement: Only a failed roll uses the helicoid. Random rotation chooses the direction around the muzzle-to-aim axis; angular error gives an offset of distance × tan(error). If the sampled ray would hit the selected part, it moves just beyond that part's outline along the same bearing. Misses can strike other body parts. The original scatter coefficients remain unchanged.

Three patterns: Angular misses uses regular scatter for every failure. Helicoid misses adds the existing wide 28–48° scatter for a natural 1. Roll-margin misses also lets the D20 margin change ordinary miss locations. All three use exactly the same hit-probability check.

Smoke caps damage only when a body hit passes through the smoke curtain. The optional bypass lifts that cap. Sample full damage is 45–55, with head ×1.5 and legs ×0.85; armor and resistance are omitted. Critical success means precise aim, not bonus damage. Damage per AP includes misses and blocked shots.

Study limits: This page supplies its own chance; live firearms calculate it from the shooter, range, selected part and other modifiers. Both use the same roll-margin miss calculation. The study target uses static ellipsoid proxies; gameplay retains its existing tactical colliders. Smoke curtains remain a study feature. The panel percentages are seeded sample results and may differ from the configured chance. Uniform random rotation means the helicoid twist does not change aggregate spread.
